output.takeaways:
Revenue Growth:
NVIDIA's revenue has accelerated dramatically, with 2024 revenues more than doubling year-on-year to $60.9B and then more than doubling again in 2025 to $130.5B. This outsized growth is being fueled by explosive demand for AI accelerators, data center compute, and leadership in high-end GPUs. The firm's unique positioning at the center of the AI compute infrastructure buildout, coupled with deep software integration (CUDA, enterprise AI stacks), gives it a durable edge and elevates its strategic relevance to hyperscalers and cloud providers. This level of growth is unprecedented in large-cap semiconductors, signaling a fundamental shift in market position—NVIDIA is transitioning from niche GPU supplier to platform leader underpinning the AI economy. For investors, this scale of revenue expansion points to both robust end-market demand and expanding TAM, underscoring the likelihood of sticky, leading market share going forward.

Gross Profit Margin:
Contribution margins have surged to 72.7% in FY24 and are expected to remain above 70% in subsequent years, following a dip to 56.9% in FY23. The margin rebound is primarily driven by pricing power on leading-edge AI GPUs, strong demand relative to supply, and operational leverage as fixed costs are spread across a rapidly growing revenue base. High gross margins reflect NVIDIA's competitive moat in proprietary architectures and its ability to monetize both hardware and software. This margin profile is materially superior to peers (AMD, INTC), highlighting sustainable differentiation and product/pricing control amid capacity constraints industry-wide. For investors, persistently elevated margins validate business quality and suggest long-term outperformance potential.

SG&A Expense Margin:
SG&A as a percentage of revenue falls sharply from 9.0% in FY23 to just 2.1% in FY26, indicating exceptional operating leverage and scalability. This decline reflects disciplined cost management even as topline expands, demonstrating management's ability to control operating expenses while investing in key growth initiatives (R&D, go-to-market). The pace of SG&A margin compression not only enhances overall profitability, but also signals effective execution—particularly impressive given the headcount and infrastructure increases necessary to support meteoric growth. For investors, rapid SG&A leverage is a strong indicator of management quality, improved cash generation, and expanding free cash flow conversion.

EBITDA Margin Stability:
NVIDIA's EBITDA margin has rocketed from 22.2% in FY23 to 66.9% in FY26, far surpassing both AMD and Intel, who remain sub-20%. This level of profitability not only reflects outstanding gross margin performance, but also best-in-class cost structure and scale efficiencies. In the peer context, NVIDIA's EV/EBITDA multiple—while elevated at the peak (81.0x in FY23)—is compressing toward 31.4x by FY26, as EBITDA scales faster than valuation expansion. This rerating enhances relative value and investment attractiveness, especially as NVIDIA sustains margin and growth levels peers cannot currently match. The combination of operational and financial excellence means NVIDIA is likely to remain a core holding for growth-oriented investors and index funds, justifying its premium valuation and status as a secular compounder.
